exposure: long-acting and permanent methods (LAPM) of contraception use
Inpatient long-acting reversible contraception (IPP LARC) use
cohort: Women who delivered in hospitals in the United States from 2012 to 2016
finding: While the rate of IPP LARC use during delivery hospitalization increased from 2012 to 2016, it remained substantially lower than the rate of PPTL use, with significant variation in uptake observed based on demographic, clinical, and geographic factors.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with greater utilization of both IPP LARC and PPTL, but the odds of PPTL use were significantly higher compared to IPP LARC among women who had a cesarean delivery (aOR 0.09, 95% CI 0.06-0.12).
